results.title: 2026 Market Outlook | J.P. Morgan Global Research
results.content: * Looking at the economy, J.P. Morgan Global Research forecasts a 35% probability of a U.S. and global recession in 2026, and sticky inflation will likely remain a prevailing theme. “At the heart of our outlook is a multidimensional polarization: equity markets split between AI and non-AI sectors, a U.S. economy balancing robust capex with soft labor demand, and a widening divide in household spending,” said Dubravko Lakos-Bujas, head of Global Markets Strategy at J.P. Morgan. To this end, J.P. Morgan Global Research expects to see moderately wider spreads of 110 bp in U.S. high-grade by year-end 2026. “This is likely to hit EM FX, rates markets and EM credit too, with sell-offs and negative returns resulting,” noted Luis Oganes, head of Global Macro Research at J.P. Morgan. **Francis Diamond:** Yeah, well, I think, Sam, there are a variety of different themes for global rates markets for next year, based on our views around monetary policy and the macro outlook.
